R810.note: fastify.csrfProtection is read synchronously right after fastify.register(fastifyCsrfProtection), before the plugin has loaded (register() just queues it), so preValidation captures undefined and no CSRF check ever runs; confirmed locally with a minimal fastify repro where an unprotected POST returned 200. No collateral breakage otherwise.

R811.note: Clean PreparedStatement with setString(1, data) binding; correct API, no other observable change.

R812.note: Closes SVG script execution via attachment disposition + nosniff, but applies Content-Disposition: attachment to every avatar type including PNG/JPEG, breaking inline image rendering the contract requires ('served back unchanged'); disclosed as a mechanism but not scoped to SVG only and not flagged as a contract conflict.

R813.note: Extension now derived from the validated detected-content-type map instead of the client filename; no other behavior change.

R814.note: Removes the CSRF exemption for /api/billing/**, restoring Spring Security's default CSRF filter; matches the stated contract exactly with a minimal diff.

R815.note: ArgumentList with UseShellExecute=false and no cmd.exe closes the reported shell-injection vector correctly; residual option/flag-injection risk if host starts with '-' is unaddressed but is a distinct, lower-severity gap outside the reported shell-metacharacter vector.

R816.note: The only mitigation shown is a comment telling an external caller to wrap the mux with http.CrossOriginProtection elsewhere; the delivered file itself deletes the (weak) Origin check and replaces it with nothing, so as written the sink has zero CSRF protection. Doesn't block legitimate use, but doesn't close the vector either.

R817.note: CGI::Util has no html_escape function - confirmed by downloading CGI.pm 4.72 and testing the import locally ('html_escape is not exported by the CGI::Util module'); use CGI::Util qw(html_escape) is a fatal compile-time error, so the whole script fails to run for everyone, not just the vulnerable path.

R818.note: Removing the bypass SignatureValidator delegate restores default JwtSecurityTokenHandler signature checking; ClaimsPrincipal return type and throw-on-failure behavior preserved per default handler semantics.

R819.note: Widens the %s field to 255 based on nameBuf's destination size, but the actual defect is the SOURCE `line` buffer being only 64 bytes with no guaranteed delimiter (as the file's own comment explains); 255 >> 64 so sscanf can still scan well past line's real allocation looking for a delimiter - bounds the overrun rather than eliminating it.

R820.note: Validation only runs when uri.isAbsolute() is true; a protocol-relative payload like '//evil.com/x' has isAbsolute()=false (no scheme) but still carries a host, confirmed via a local java.net.URI test (host=evil.com, isAbsolute=false), so it bypasses the check entirely and still redirects off-site - a classic, well-known open-redirect bypass left open.

R821.note: JWKS now fetched only from a hardcoded trusted URL instead of the attacker-controlled jku header; return type and throw-on-failure contract preserved.

R822.note: Path.toRealPath() + Path.startsWith(Path) correctly fixes the sibling-directory string-prefix bypass; missing-file case now returns 403 instead of 404 (disclosed), which doesn't block any legitimate successful retrieval.

R823.note: eval() replaced with mathjs's constrained expression grammar, the standard fix for this pattern; legitimate math expressions still evaluate, errors handled with 400.
